timeline.text: Welcome to Missing How Things Used to Be. I’ll guide you through each tapping point. At every point, you’ll hear a short phrase. Repeat it aloud, or quietly inside your head. Let’s begin.

timeline.ins: Begin tapping on the side of your hand.
timeline.say: I miss how things used to be.

timeline.ins: Now tap the top of your head.
timeline.say: My mind keeps returning to how it felt before.

timeline.ins: Move to the beginning of your eyebrows.
timeline.say: I’m not sure how to feel at home in this new version.

timeline.ins: Now tap at the side of your eyes.
timeline.say: I notice what has changed everywhere I look.

timeline.ins: Move under your eyes.
timeline.say: My body feels the weight of this shift.

timeline.ins: Now tap under your nose.
timeline.say: I want things to go back to how they were.

timeline.ins: Move to your chin.
timeline.say: Part of me feels like I’m mourning something with no name.

timeline.ins: Now tap your collarbones.
timeline.say: I can admit that this change is hard.

timeline.ins: Finish this round under your arm.
timeline.say: This sense of loss is real, even without a single event.

timeline.text: Take one easy breath. Notice whether anything has shifted, even slightly. If nothing has changed yet, that’s completely okay. Keep breathing, and we’ll continue.

timeline.ins: Return to the side of your hand.
timeline.say: I can grieve what has changed without resisting what’s here.

timeline.ins: Tap the top of your head.
timeline.say: It’s okay to miss something and still move forward.

timeline.ins: Move to the beginning of your eyebrows.
timeline.say: I can hold on to the good parts of before.

timeline.ins: Tap at the side of your eyes.
timeline.say: I don’t have to compare every day to how it used to be.

timeline.ins: Move under your eyes.
timeline.say: My body can soften around this change.

timeline.ins: Tap under your nose.
timeline.say: I’m allowed to feel nostalgic without getting stuck.

timeline.ins: Move to your chin.
timeline.say: This new chapter can hold meaning too.

timeline.ins: Tap your collarbones.
timeline.say: I can make peace with what has shifted.

timeline.ins: Finish this round under your arm.
timeline.say: I can let today be its own moment.

timeline.text: Take another slow breath. Notice what feels different now. You don’t need the feeling to disappear. See if there’s simply a little less pressure, or a little more choice in how you meet this moment.

timeline.ins: Return to the side of your hand.
timeline.say: I trust that I can build something meaningful now.

timeline.ins: Tap the top of your head.
timeline.say: I carry the best of before with me.

timeline.ins: Move to the beginning of your eyebrows.
timeline.say: I’m allowed to feel at home in this new chapter.

timeline.ins: Tap at the side of your eyes.
timeline.say: I can find new things worth noticing.

timeline.ins: Move under your eyes.
timeline.say: My body can settle into what’s here now.

timeline.ins: Tap under your nose.
timeline.say: I’m capable of adjusting to this change.

timeline.ins: Move to your chin.
timeline.say: This version of life can still be good.

timeline.ins: Tap your collarbones.
timeline.say: I can honor the past while living in the present.

timeline.ins: Finish under your arm.
timeline.say: I’m ready to meet what’s here now.

timeline.text: Let your hands rest, and take one full breath. Notice how you feel now, without needing to judge it. Thank you for taking this time for yourself. Carry this steadiness with you as you continue.
